That is consistent with the 47-crossing Khovanov complex not fitting in 15 GB, but it is not established: no attempt has captured an exit code or an OOM message, so 'ran out of memory' remains the leading hypothesis rather than a finding. instrumentation_gap.what_broke: The watch used `pgrep -f KnotJob.jar`, which matched the watcher's own shell command line because that string appears in the command. The process-exited branch could therefore never fire, and the death was not noticed until an hourly check-in read `ps -C java` and found nothing.
instrumentation_gap.consequence: One status report in this session said the run was alive after it had already died.
instrumentation_gap.fix: scripts/run_knotjob_watched.sh records the pid, exit code and wall time to a sidecar file, so a silent death is recorded as a death rather than inferred from an absence.
